numbering: Standard 700-verse canon; Chapter 13 has 34 verses and excludes Arjuna's alternate opening question.
sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Arjuna.
2:   Thou whom all mortals praise, Janardana!
3:   If meditation be a nobler thing
4:   Than action, wherefore, then, great Kesava!
5:   Dost thou impel me to this dreadful fight?
6:   Now am I by thy doubtful speech disturbed!
7:   Tell me one thing, and tell me certainly;
8:   By what road shall I find the better end?
9: 
10:   Krishna.
11:   I told thee, blameless Lord! there be two paths
12:   Shown to this world; two schools of wisdom.
13: 
14:   First
15:   The Sankhya's, which doth save in way of works
16:   Prescribed[FN#4] by reason; next, the Yog, which bids
17:   Attain by meditation, spiritually:
18:   Yet these are one! No man shall 'scape from act
19:   By shunning action; nay, and none shall come
20:   By mere renouncements unto perfectness.
21:   Nay, and no jot of time, at any time,
22:   Rests any actionless; his nature's law
23:   Compels him, even unwilling, into act;
24:   [For thought is act in fancy]. He who sits
25:   Suppressing all the instruments of flesh,
26:   Yet in his idle heart thinking on them,
27:   Plays the inept and guilty hypocrite:
28:   But he who, with strong body serving mind,
29:   Gives up his mortal powers to worthy work,
30:   Not seeking gain, Arjuna! such an one
31:   Is honourable. Do thine allotted task!
32:   Work is more excellent than idleness;
33:   The body's life proceeds not, lacking work.
34:   There is a task of holiness to do,
35:   Unlike world-binding toil, which bindeth not
36:   The faithful soul; such earthly duty do
37:   Free from desire, and thou shalt well perform
38:   Thy heavenly purpose. Spake Prajapati--
39:   In the beginning, when all men were made,
40:   And, with mankind, the sacrifice-- "Do this!
41:   Work! sacrifice! Increase and multiply
42:   With sacrifice! This shall be Kamaduk,
43:   Your 'Cow of Plenty,' giving back her milk
44:   Of all abundance. Worship the gods thereby;
45:   The gods shall yield thee grace. Those meats ye crave
46:   The gods will grant to Labour, when it pays
47:   Tithes in the altar-flame. But if one eats
48:   Fruits of the earth, rendering to kindly Heaven
49:   No gift of toil, that thief steals from his world."
50: 
51:   Who eat of food after their sacrifice
52:   Are quit of fault, but they that spread a feast
53:   All for themselves, eat sin and drink of sin.
54:   By food the living live; food comes of rain,
55:   And rain comes by the pious sacrifice,
56:   And sacrifice is paid with tithes of toil;
57:   Thus action is of Brahma, who is One,
58:   The Only, All-pervading; at all times
59:   Present in sacrifice. He that abstains
60:   To help the rolling wheels of this great world,
61:   Glutting his idle sense, lives a lost life,
62:   Shameful and vain. Existing for himself,
63:   Self-concentrated, serving self alone,
64:   No part hath he in aught; nothing achieved,
65:   Nought wrought or unwrought toucheth him; no hope
66:   Of help for all the living things of earth
67:   Depends from him.[FN#5] Therefore, thy task prescribed
68:   With spirit unattached gladly perform,
69:   Since in performance of plain duty man
70:   Mounts to his highest bliss. By works alone
71:   Janak and ancient saints reached blessedness!
72:   Moreover, for the upholding of thy kind,
73:   Action thou should'st embrace. What the wise choose
74:   The unwise people take; what best men do
75:   The multitude will follow. Look on me,
76:   Thou Son of Pritha! in the three wide worlds
77:   I am not bound to any toil, no height
78:   Awaits to scale, no gift remains to gain,
79:   Yet I act here! and, if I acted not--
80:   Earnest and watchful--those that look to me
81:   For guidance, sinking back to sloth again
82:   Because I slumbered, would decline from good,
83:   And I should break earth's order and commit
84:   Her offspring unto ruin, Bharata!
85:   Even as the unknowing toil, wedded to sense,
86:   So let the enlightened toil, sense-freed, but set
87:   To bring the world deliverance, and its bliss;
88:   Not sowing in those simple, busy hearts
89:   Seed of despair. Yea! let each play his part
90:   In all he finds to do, with unyoked soul.
91:   All things are everywhere by Nature wrought
92:   In interaction of the qualities.
93:   The fool, cheated by self, thinks, "This I did"
94:   And "That I wrought; "but--ah, thou strong-armed Prince!--
95:   A better-lessoned mind, knowing the play
96:   Of visible things within the world of sense,
97:   And how the qualities must qualify,
98:   Standeth aloof even from his acts. Th' untaught
99:   Live mixed with them, knowing not Nature's way,
100:   Of highest aims unwitting, slow and dull.
101:   Those make thou not to stumble, having the light;
102:   But all thy dues discharging, for My sake,
103:   With meditation centred inwardly,
104:   Seeking no profit, satisfied, serene,
105:   Heedless of issue--fight! They who shall keep
106:   My ordinance thus, the wise and willing hearts,
107:   Have quittance from all issue of their acts;
108:   But those who disregard My ordinance,
109:   Thinking they know, know nought, and fall to loss,
110:   Confused and foolish. 'Sooth, the instructed one
111:   Doth of his kind, following what fits him most:
112:   And lower creatures of their kind; in vain
113:   Contending 'gainst the law. Needs must it be
114:   The objects of the sense will stir the sense
115:   To like and dislike, yet th' enlightened man
116:   Yields not to these, knowing them enemies.
117:   Finally, this is better, that one do
118:   His own task as he may, even though he fail,
119:   Than take tasks not his own, though they seem good.
120:   To die performing duty is no ill;
121:   But who seeks other roads shall wander still.
122: 
123:   Arjuna.
124:   Yet tell me, Teacher! by what force doth man
125:   Go to his ill, unwilling; as if one
126:   Pushed him that evil path?
127: 
128:   Krishna.
129:   Kama it is!
130:   Passion it is! born of the Darknesses,
131:   Which pusheth him. Mighty of appetite,
132:   Sinful, and strong is this!--man's enemy!
133:   As smoke blots the white fire, as clinging rust
134:   Mars the bright mirror, as the womb surrounds
135:   The babe unborn, so is the world of things
136:   Foiled, soiled, enclosed in this desire of flesh.
137:   The wise fall, caught in it; the unresting foe
138:   It is of wisdom, wearing countless forms,
139:   Fair but deceitful, subtle as a flame.
140:   Sense, mind, and reason--these, O Kunti's Son!
141:   Are booty for it; in its play with these
142:   It maddens man, beguiling, blinding him.
143:   Therefore, thou noblest child of Bharata!
144:   Govern thy heart! Constrain th' entangled sense!
145:   Resist the false, soft sinfulness which saps
146:   Knowledge and judgment! Yea, the world is strong,
147:   But what discerns it stronger, and the mind
148:   Strongest; and high o'er all the ruling Soul.
149:   Wherefore, perceiving Him who reigns supreme,
150:   Put forth full force of Soul in thy own soul!
151:   Fight! vanquish foes and doubts, dear Hero! slay
152:   What haunts thee in fond shapes, and would betray!
153: 
154:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER III. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
155:   Entitled "Karma-Yog,"
156:   Or "The Book of Virtue in Work."

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
records.iast:
arjuna uvāca
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  Thou whom all mortals praise, Janardana!
  If meditation be a nobler thing
  Than action, wherefore, then, great Kesava!
  Dost thou impel me to this dreadful fight?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.1 Arjuna said If Thou thinkest that knowledge is superior to action, O Krishna, why then, O Kesava, dost Thou ask me to engage in this terrible action?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.1 "Arjuna questioned: My Lord! If Wisdom is above action, why dost Thou advise me to engage in this terrible fight?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.1 Arjuna said O Janardana (krsna), if it be Your opinion that wisdom is superior to action, why they do you urge me to horrible aciton, O Kesava ?

records.sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
records.iast:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me
tadekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo.ahamāpnuyām
records.speaker: Arjuna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.2 With this apparently perplexing speech, Thou confusest, as it were, my understanding; therefore tell me that one way for certain by which I may attain bliss.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.2 Thy language perplexes me and confuses my reason. Therefore please tell me the only way by which I may, without doubt, secure my spiritual welfare.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.2 You bewilder my understanding, as it were, by a seemingly conflicting statement! Tell me for certain one of these by which I may attain the highest Good.

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
loke.asmina dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
jñānayogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  I told thee, blameless Lord! there be two paths
  Shown to this world; two schools of wisdom.

  First
  The Sankhya's, which doth save in way of works
  Prescribed[FN#4] by reason; next, the Yog, which bids
  Attain by meditation, spiritually:
  Yet these are one!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.3 The Blessed Lord said In this world there is a twofold path, as I said before, O sinless one; the path of knowledge of the Sankhyas and the path of action of the Yogins.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.3 Lord Shri Krishna replied: In this world, as I have said, there is a twofold path, O Sinless One! There is the Path of Wisdom for those who meditate, and the Path of Action for those who work.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.3 The Blessed Lord said O unblemished one, two kinds of steadfastness in this world were spoken of by Me in the days of yore-through the Yoga of Knowledge for the men of realization; through the Yoga of Action for the yogis.

records.sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
records.iast:
na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo.aśnute
na ca saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
No man shall 'scape from act
  By shunning action; nay, and none shall come
  By mere renouncements unto perfectness.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.4 Not by non-performance of actions does man reach actionlessness; nor by mere renunciation does he attain to perfection.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.4 No man can attain freedom from activity by refraining from action; nor can he reach perfection by merely refusing to act.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.4 A person does not attain freedom from action by abstaining from action; nor does he attain fulfilment merely through renunciation.

records.sanskrit:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
records.iast:
na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt
kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Nay, and no jot of time, at any time,
  Rests any actionless; his nature's law
  Compels him, even unwilling, into act;
  [For thought is act in fancy].

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.5 Verily none can ever remain for even a moment without performing action; for everyone is made to act helplessly indeed by the alities born of Nature.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.5 He cannot even for a moment remain really inactive, for the Qualities of Nature will compel him to act whether he will or no.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.5 Because, no one ever remains even for a moment without doing work. For all are made to work under compulsion by the gunas born of Nature.

records.sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
records.iast:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who sits
  Suppressing all the instruments of flesh,
  Yet in his idle heart thinking on them,
  Plays the inept and guilty hypocrite:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.6 He who, restraining the organs of action, sits thinking of the sense-objects in mind, he of deluded understanding is called a hypocrite.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.6 He who remains motionless, refusing to act, but all the while brooding over sensuous object, that deluded soul is simply a hypocrite.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.6 One, who after withdrawing the organs of action, sits mentally recollecting the objects of the senses, that one, of deluded mind, is called a hypocrite.

records.sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
records.iast:
yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate.arjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But he who, with strong body serving mind,
  Gives up his mortal powers to worthy work,
  Not seeking gain, Arjuna! such an one
  Is honourable.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.7 But whosoever, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, engages himself in Karma Yoga with the organs of action, without attachment, he excels.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.7 But, O Arjuna! All honour to him whose mind controls his senses, for he is thereby beginning to practise Karma-Yoga, the Path of Right Action, keeping himself always unattached.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.7 But, O Arjuna, one who engages in Karma-yoga with the organs of action, controlling the organs with the mind and becoming unattached-that one excels.

records.sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
records.iast:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.8 Do thou perform (thy) bounden duty, for action is superior to inaction and even the maintenance of the body would not be possible for thee by inaction.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.8 Do thy duty as prescribed, for action for duty's sake is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if man remained inactive.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.8 You perform the obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. And, through inaction, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible.

records.sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥
records.iast:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo.anyatra loko.ayaṃ karmabandhanaḥ
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
There is a task of holiness to do,
  Unlike world-binding toil, which bindeth not
  The faithful soul; such earthly duty do
  Free from desire, and thou shalt well perform
  Thy heavenly purpose.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.9 The world is bound by actions other than those performed for the sake of sacrifice; do thou, therefore, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), perform action for that sake (for sacrifice alone), free from attachment.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.9 In this world people are fettered by action, unless it is performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let thy acts be done without attachment, as sacrifice only.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.9 This man becomes bound by actions other than that action meant for God. Without being attached, O son of Kunti, you perform actions for Him.

records.sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
records.iast:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Spake Prajapati--
  In the beginning, when all men were made,
  And, with mankind, the sacrifice-- "Do this!
  Work! sacrifice! Increase and multiply
  With sacrifice! This shall be Kamaduk,
  Your 'Cow of Plenty,' giving back her milk
  Of all abundance.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.10 The Creator, having in the beginning (of creation) created mankind together with sacrifice, said, "By this shall ye propagate; let this be the milch cow of your desires (the cow which yields all the desired objects)."

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.10 In the beginning, when God created all beings by the sacrifice of Himself, He said unto them: Through sacrifice you can procreate, and it shall satisfy all your desires.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.10 In the days of yore, having created the beings together with the sacrifices, Prajapati said: 'By this you multiply. Let this be your yielder of coveted objects of desire.'

records.sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
records.iast:
devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Worship the gods thereby;
  The gods shall yield thee grace.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.11 With this do ye nourish the gods and may those gods nourish you; thus nourishing one another, ye shall attain to the highest good.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.11 Worship the Powers of Nature thereby, and let them nourish you in return; thus supporting each other, you shall attain your highest welfare.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.11 'You nourish the gods with this. Let those gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you shall attain the supreme Good.'

records.sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
records.iast:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Those meats ye crave
  The gods will grant to Labour, when it pays
  Tithes in the altar-flame. But if one eats
  Fruits of the earth, rendering to kindly Heaven

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.12 The gods, nourished by the sacrifice, will give you the desired objects. So, he who enjoys the objects given by the gods without offering (in return) to them, is verily a thief.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.12 For, fed, on sacrifice, nature will give you all the enjoyment you can desire. But he who enjoys what she gives without returning is, indeed, a robber.'

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.12 'Being nourished by sacrifices, the gods will indeed give you the coveted enjoyments. He is certainly a theif who enjoys what have been given by them without offering (these) to them.'

records.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
records.iast:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Who eat of food after their sacrifice
  Are quit of fault, but they that spread a feast
  All for themselves, eat sin and drink of sin.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.13 The righteous who eat the remnants of the sacrifice are freed from all sins; but those sinful ones who cook food (only) for their own sake verily eat sin.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.13 The sages who enjoy the food that remains after the sacrifice is made are freed from all sin; but the selfish who spread their feast only for themselves feed on sin only.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.13 By becoming partakers of the remembers of sacrifices, they become freed from all sins. But the unholy persons who cook for themselves, they incur sin.

records.sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
records.iast:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.14 From food come forth beings; from rain food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain and sacrifice is born of action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.14 All creatures are the product of food, food is the product of rain, rain comes by sacrifice, and sacrifice is the noblest form of action.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.14 From food are born the creatures; the origin of food is from rainfall; rainfall originates from sacrifice; sacrifice has action as its origin.

records.sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
records.iast:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Thus action is of Brahma, who is One,
  The Only, All-pervading; at all times
  Present in sacrifice.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.15 Know thou that action comes from Brahma and Brahma comes from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading (Brahma) ever rests in sacrifice.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.15 All action originates in the Supreme Spirit, which is Imperishable, and in sacrificial action the all-pervading Spirit is consciously present.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.15 Know that actin has the veda as its origin; the Vedas has the Immutable as its source. Hence, the all-pervading Veda is for ever based on sacrifice.

records.sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
records.iast:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He that abstains
  To help the rolling wheels of this great world,
  Glutting his idle sense, lives a lost life,
  Shameful and vain.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.16 He who does not follow here the wheel thus set revolving, who is of sinful life, rejoicing in the senses, he lives in vain, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.16 Thus he who does not help the revolving wheel of sacrifice, but instead leads a sinful life, rejoicing in the gratification of his senses, O Arjuna, he breathes in vain.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.16 O Partha, he lives in vain who does not follow here the wheel thus set in motion, whose life is sinful, and who indulges in the senses.

records.sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
records.iast:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.17 But for that man who rejoices only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self and who is content in the Self alone, verily there is nothing to do.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.17 On the other hand, the soul who meditates on the Self is content to serve the Self and rests satisfied within the Self; there remains nothing more for him to accomplish.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.17 But that man who rejoices only in theSelf and is satisfied with the Self, and is contented only in the Self-for him there is no duty to perform.

records.sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
records.iast:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
nothing achieved,
  Nought wrought or unwrought toucheth him; no hope
  Of help for all the living things of earth
  Depends from him.[FN#5]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.18 For him there is no interest whatever in what is done or what is not done; nor does he depend on any being for any object.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.18 He has nothing to gain by the performance or non-performance of action. His welfare depends not on any contribution that an earthly creature can make.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.18 For him there is no concern here at all with performing action; nor any (concern) with nonperformance. Moreover, for him there is no dependence on any object to serve any purpose.

records.sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
records.iast:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Therefore, thy task prescribed
  With spirit unattached gladly perform,
  Since in performance of plain duty man
  Mounts to his highest bliss.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.19 Therefore without attachment, do thou always perform action which should be done; for by performing action without attachment man reaches the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.19 Therefore do thy duty perfectly, without care for the results, for he who does his duty disinterestedly attains the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.19 Therefore, remaining unattached, always perform the obligatory duty, for, by performing (one's) duty without attachment, a person attains the Highest.

records.sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
records.iast:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ
lokasaṃgrahamevāpi sampaśyankartumarhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
By works alone
  Janak and ancient saints reached blessedness!
  Moreover, for the upholding of thy kind,
  Action thou should'st embrace.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.20 Janaka and others attained perfection verily by action only; even with a view to the protection of the masses thou shouldst perform action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.20 King Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of enlightening the world, it is thy duty to act;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.20 For Janaka and others strove to attain Liberation through action itself. You ought to perform (your duties) keeping also in view the prevention of mankind from going astray.

records.sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
records.iast:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
What the wise choose
  The unwise people take; what best men do
  The multitude will follow.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.21 Whatsoever a great man does, that the other men also do; whatever he sets up as the standard, that the world (mankind) follows.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.21 For whatever a great man does, others imitate. People conform to the standard which he has set.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.21 Whatever a superior person does, another person does that very thing! Whatever he upholds as authority, an ordinary person follows that.

records.sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
records.iast:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana
nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Look on me,
  Thou Son of Pritha! in the three wide worlds
  I am not bound to any toil, no height
  Awaits to scale, no gift remains to gain,
  Yet I act here!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.22 There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, that should be done by Me, nor is there anything unattained that should be attained; yet I engage Myself in action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.22 There is nothing in this universe, O Arjuna, that I am compelled to do, nor anything for Me to attain; yet I am persistently active.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.22 In all the three worlds, O Partha, there is no duty whatsoever for Me (to fulfil); nothing remains unachieved or to be achieved. [According to S. the translation of this portion is: There is nothing unattained that should be attained.-Tr.] (Still) do I continue in action.

records.sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
records.iast:
yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
and, if I acted not--
  Earnest and watchful--those that look to me
  For guidance, sinking back to sloth again
  Because I slumbered, would decline from good,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.23 For, should I not ever engage Myself in action, unwearied, men would in every way follow My path, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.23 For were I not to act without ceasing, O prince, people would be glad to do likewise.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.23 For, O Partha, if at any time I do not continue [Ast. and A.A. read varteya instead of varteyam.-Tr.] vigilantly in action, men will follow My path in ever way.

records.sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
records.iast:
utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham
saṅkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And I should break earth's order and commit
  Her offspring unto ruin, Bharata!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.24 These worlds would perish if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes and destruction of these beings.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.24 And if I were to refrain from action, the human race would be ruined; I should lead the world to chaos, and destruction would follow.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.24 These worlds will be ruined if I do not perform action. And I shall become the agent of intermingling (of castes), and shall be destroying these beings.

records.sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥
records.iast:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryādvidvāṃstathāsaktaścikīrṣurlokasaṃgraham
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.25 As the ignorant men act from attachment to action, O Bharata (Arjuna), so should the wise act without attachment, wishing the welfare of the world.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.25 As the ignorant act, because of their fondness for action, so should the wise act without such attachment, fixing their eyes, O Arjuna, only on the welfare of the world.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.25 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, as the unelightened poeple act with attachment to work, so should the enlightened person act, without attachment, being desirous of the prevention of people from going astray.

records.sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
records.iast:
na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām
joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvānyuktaḥ samācaran
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Not sowing in those simple, busy hearts
  Seed of despair. Yea! let each play his part
  In all he finds to do, with unyoked soul.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.26 Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people who are attached to action; he should engage them in all actions, himself fulfilling them with devotion.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.26 But a wise man should not perturb the minds of the ignorant, who are attached to action; let him perform his own actions in the right spirit, with concentration on Me, thus inspiring all to do the same.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.26 The enlightened man should not create disturbance in the beliefs of the ignorant, who are attached to work. Working, while himself remaining deligen [Some translate yuktah as, 'in the right manner'. S. takes it in the sense of Yoga-yuktah, merged in yoga.-Tr.], he should make them do [Another reading is yojayet, meaning the same as josayet.-Tr.] all the duties.

records.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते ॥
records.iast:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ
ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartāhamiti manyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
All things are everywhere by Nature wrought
  In interaction of the qualities.
  The fool, cheated by self, thinks, "This I did"
  And "That I wrought; "

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.27 All actions are wrought in all cases by the alities of Nature only. He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.27 Action is the product of the Qualities inherent in Nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says: I am the doer.'

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.27 While actions are being done in every way by the gunas (alities) of Nature, one who is deluded by egoism thinks thus: 'I am the doer.'

records.sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
records.iast:
tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
but--ah, thou strong-armed Prince!--
  A better-lessoned mind, knowing the play
  Of visible things within the world of sense,
  And how the qualities must qualify,
  Standeth aloof even from his acts.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.28 But he who knows the Truth, O mighty-armed (Arjuna), about the divisions of the alities and (their) functions, knowing that the Gunas as senses move amidst the Gunas as the sense-objects, is not attached.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.28 But he, O Mighty One, who understands correctly the relation of the Qualities to action, is not attached to the act for he perceives that it is merely the action and reaction of the Qualities among themselves.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.28 But, O mighty-armed one, the one who is a knower of the facts about the varieties of the gunas (alities) and actions does not become attached, thinking thus: 'The organs rest (act) on the objects of the organs.'

records.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥
records.iast:
prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu
tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Th' untaught
  Live mixed with them, knowing not Nature's way,
  Of highest aims unwitting, slow and dull.
  Those make thou not to stumble, having the light;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.29 Those deluded by the alities of Nature are attached to the functions of the alities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish one who is of imperfect knowledge.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.29 Those who do not understand the Qualities are interested in the act. Still, the wise man who knows the truth should not disturb the mind of him who does not.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.29 Those who are wholly deluded by the gunas of Nature become attached to the activities of the gunas. The knower of the All should not disturb those of dull intellect, who do not know the All.

records.sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
records.iast:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But all thy dues discharging, for My sake,
  With meditation centred inwardly,
  Seeking no profit, satisfied, serene,
  Heedless of issue--fight!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.30 Renouncing all actions in Me, with the mind centred in the Self, free from hope and egoism, and from (mental) fever, do thou fight.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.30 Therefore, surrendering thy actions unto Me, thy thoughts concentrated on the Absolute, free from selfishness and without anticipation of reward, with mind devoid of excitement, begin thou to fight.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.30 Devoid of the fever of the soul, engage in battle by dedicating all actions to Me, with (your) mind intent on the Self, and becoming free from expectations and egoism.

records.sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
records.iast:
ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ
śraddhāvanto.anasūyanto mucyante te.api karmabhiḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.31 Those men who constantly practise this teaching of Mine with faith and without cavilling, they too are freed from actions.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.31 Those who always act in accordance with My precepts, firm in faith and without cavilling, they too are freed from the bondage of action.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.31 Those men who ever follow this teaching of Mine with faith and without cavil, they also become freed from actions.

records.sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
records.iast:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But those who disregard My ordinance,
  Thinking they know, know nought, and fall to loss,
  Confused and foolish.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.32 But those who carp at My teaching and do not practise it, deluded of all knowledge, and devoid of discrimination, know them to be doomed to destruction.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.32 But they who ridicule My word and do not keep it, are ignorant, devoid of wisdom and blind. They seek but their own destruction.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.32 But those who, decaying [Finding fault where there is none.] this, do not follow My teaching, know them-who are deluded about all knoweldge [Knowledge concerning the alified and the un-alified Brahman.] and who are devoid of discrimination-to have gone to ruin.

records.sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
records.iast:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
'Sooth, the instructed one
  Doth of his kind, following what fits him most:
  And lower creatures of their kind; in vain
  Contending 'gainst the law.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
3.33 Even a wise man acts in accordance with his own nature; beings will follow Nature; what can
restraint do?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.33 Even the wise man acts in character with his nature; indeed, all creatures act according to their natures. What is the use of compulsion then?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.33 Even a man of wisdom behaves according to his own nature. Being follow (their) nature. What can restraint do?

records.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
records.iast:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Needs must it be
  The objects of the sense will stir the sense
  To like and dislike, yet th' enlightened man
  Yields not to these, knowing them enemies.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.34 Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses; let none come under their sway; for, they are his foes.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.34 The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them. They only obstruct the path.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.34 Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

records.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
records.iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Finally, this is better, that one do
  His own task as he may, even though he fail,
  Than take tasks not his own, though they seem good.
  To die performing duty is no ill;
  But who seeks other roads shall wander still.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.35 Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit than the duty of another well discharged. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear (is productive of danger).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.35 It is better to do thine own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing one's own duty, for to do the duty of another is fraught with danger.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.35 One's own duty [Customary or scripturally ordained observances of different castes and sects.-Tr.], though defective, is superior to another's duty well-performed. Death is better while engaged in one's own duty; another's duty is fraught with fear.

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
records.iast:
arjuna uvāca
atha kena prayukto.ayaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  Yet tell me, Teacher! by what force doth man
  Go to his ill, unwilling; as if one
  Pushed him that evil path?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.36 Arjuna said But impelled by what does man commit sin, though against his wishes, O Varshneya (Krishna), constrained as it were, by force?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.36 Arjuna asked: My Lord! Tell me, what is it that drives a man to sin, even against his will and as if by compulsion?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.36 Arjuna said Now then, O scion of the Vrsni dynasty (Krsna), impelled by what does this man commit sin even against his wish, being constrained by force, as it were?

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  Kama it is!
  Passion it is! born of the Darknesses,
  Which pusheth him. Mighty of appetite,
  Sinful, and strong is this!--man's enemy!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.37 The Blessed Lord said It is desire, it is anger both of the ality of Rajas, all-devouring, all-sinful; know this as the foe here (in this world).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.37 Lord Shri Krishna: It is desire, it is aversion, born of passion. Desire consumes and corrupts everything. It is man's greatest enemy.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.37 The Blessed Lord said This desire, this anger, born of the ality of rajas, is a great devourer, a great sinner. Know this to be the enemy here.

records.sanskrit:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
records.iast:
dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathādarśo malena ca
yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
As smoke blots the white fire, as clinging rust
  Mars the bright mirror, as the womb surrounds
  The babe unborn, so is the world of things
  Foiled, soiled, enclosed in this desire of flesh.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.38 As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, and as an embryo by the amnion, so is this enveloped by that.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.38 As fire is shrouded in smoke, a mirror by dust and a child by the womb, so is the universe enveloped in desire.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.38 As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dirt, and as a foetus remains enclosed in the womb, so in this shrouded by that.

records.sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
records.iast:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā
kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The wise fall, caught in it; the unresting foe
  It is of wisdom, wearing countless forms,
  Fair but deceitful, subtle as a flame.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.39 O Arjuna, wisdom is enveloped by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is unappeasable as fire.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.39 It is the wise man's constant enemy; it tarnishes the face of wisdom. It is as insatiable as a flame of fire.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.39 O son of Kunti, Knowledge is covered by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is an insatiable fire.

records.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
records.iast:
indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate
etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Sense, mind, and reason--these, O Kunti's Son!
  Are booty for it; in its play with these
  It maddens man, beguiling, blinding him.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.40 The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these it deludes the embodied by veiling his wisdom.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.40 It works through the senses, the mind and the reason; and with their help destroys wisdom and confounds the soul.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.40 The organs, mind, and the intellect are said to be its abode. This one diversely deludes the embodied being by veiling Knowledge with the help of these.

records.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
records.iast:
tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Therefore, thou noblest child of Bharata!
  Govern thy heart! Constrain th' entangled sense!
  Resist the false, soft sinfulness which saps
  Knowledge and judgment!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.41 Therefore, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), controlling the senses first, do thou kill this sinful thing, the destroyer of knowledge and realisation.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.41 Therefore, O Arjuna, first control thy senses and then slay desire, for it is full of sin, and is the destroyer of knowledge and of wisdom.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.41 Therefore, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, after first controlling the organs, renounce this one [A variant reading is, 'prajahi hi-enam, completely renounce this one'.-Tr.] which is sinful and a destroyer of learning and wisdom.

records.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
records.iast:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ
manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yea, the world is strong,
  But what discerns it stronger, and the mind
  Strongest; and high o'er all the ruling Soul.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.42 They say that the senses are superior (to the body); superior to the senses is the mind; superior to the mind is the intellect; one who is superior even to the intellect is He (the Self).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.42 It is said that the senses are powerful. But beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and beyond and greater than intellect is He.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.42 They say that the organs are superior (to the gross body); the mind is superior to the organs; but the intellect is superior to the mind. However, the one who is superior to the intellect is He.

records.sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
records.iast:
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānamātmanā
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Wherefore, perceiving Him who reigns supreme,
  Put forth full force of Soul in thy own soul!
  Fight! vanquish foes and doubts, dear Hero! slay
  What haunts thee in fond shapes, and would betray!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 3.43 Thus knowing Him Who is superior to the intellect and restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the enemy in the form of desire, hard to coner.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 3.43 Thus, O Mighty-in-Arms, knowing Him to be beyond the intellect and, by His help, subduing thy personal egotism, kill thine enemy, Desire, extremely difficult though it be."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 3.43 [The Ast, introdcues this verse with, 'Tatah kim, what follows from that?'-Tr.] Understanding the Self thus [Understanding৷৷.thus:that desires can be conered through the knowledge of the Self.] as superior to the intellect, and completely establishing (the Self) is spiritual absorption with the (help of) the mind, O mighty-armed one, vanish the enemy in the form of desire, which is difficult to subdue.
